_activity: Match the question to its thesis
intro: Match each question to the thesis that answers it. A thesis is a claim somebody could argue with.

left.label: Were the colonists right to resist the Stamp Act?
Did the Declaration's promise of equality include everyone?
Was the government under the Articles strong enough?
Did the Bill of Rights answer the Anti-Federalists?
Did the Sedition Act break the First Amendment?

right.label: The colonists were right to resist, because Parliament taxed them without any representatives of their own.
Although it said all men are created equal, the Declaration left out enslaved people and women.
The Articles were too weak to work, because Congress could not tax or make the states act.
The Bill of Rights answered most Anti-Federalist fears by putting limits on the national government in writing.
The Sedition Act went against the First Amendment, because it jailed people for criticizing the government.

rationale.a: It takes a side (right to resist) and gives a reason (no representatives).
rationale.b: It answers the question with a claim, and “although” shows the other side.
rationale.c: A clear no, with two reasons from Document 11.
rationale.d: It takes a position (it answered most fears) and says how.
rationale.e: A clear yes, with the reason: speech and press were punished.

a: Which thesis is about a tax?
b: Look for who was left out.
c: Which thesis is about the Articles?
Look for Congress not being able to tax.
e: Which thesis is about jailing critics?
